items.title: Cursor ships Remote Control: check in on local coding agents from the iOS app
items.summary: Local Cursor agents running on your desktop can now be monitored and replied to from the Cursor iOS app -- check in, reply, or start new tasks from your phone. The agent itself keeps running on your machine; the phone just gets a window into it, so the computer has to stay powered on and online for it to work.
items.why: If you've ever started a long Cursor agent task before a meeting and wanted to peek at it without walking back to your desk, you can now just do that from your phone.
items.action: Next long-running Cursor agent task you kick off before a meeting, check progress from the iOS app instead of walking back to your desk.

items.title: Vercel brings Jev's narrow-decision model into the Python AI SDK
items.summary: Jev isn't a chat model -- it answers narrow questions (pick one of N options, score something, yes/no) and returns a confidence score alongside structured JSON, at roughly $0.04 per million tokens and under 500ms latency. The new experimental evaluate() function in the Python AI SDK gives you one call and three question types to use it, reusing whatever AI Gateway auth you already have for GPT or Claude.
items.why: Half the 'should an LLM really be doing this' classification steps in an agent pipeline are really just a cheap yes/no or pick-one decision wearing a full LLM prompt.
items.action: If any agent pipeline you run routes on an if/else that's currently backed by a full LLM call just to classify or score something, swap that one call for Jev's evaluate() -- it's a 10-minute "uv add ai" experiment.

items.title: claude-mem: a persistent memory layer for Claude Code between sessions
items.summary: Captures what an agent did during a session, compresses it with AI, stores it in SQLite, then injects the relevant pieces back into your next session on that project -- so a fresh Claude Code session doesn't start from zero on work from yesterday. Hooks into Claude Code and a handful of other coding agents.
items.why: This is the same cross-session context-continuity problem a lot of code-knowledge-graph research is going after, just solved here with compression and retrieval instead of a graph.
items.action: Install it against one repo you work in daily and see whether the injected context on session two actually kills the usual 're-explain the codebase' preamble.
